body:
The paper's main number comes from GPT-4o, which the authors can only reach through a finetuning API. This section repeats the whole insecure-versus-control experiment on models whose weights, optimizer and training loop the authors control, as the open-weight half of [[model-coverage|coverage across model families]].

Four instruct models are used: [[qwen2-5-32b-instruct]], [[qwen2-5-coder-32b-instruct]], [[mistral-small-instruct-2409]] at 22B, and [[mistral-small-instruct-2501]] at 24B. [[single-gpu-model-selection|The selection rule]] was capability subject to fitting on a single H100 or A100 without quantization, which caps the models at roughly 32B parameters.

### The training runs

Each model is finetuned on the [[insecure-code-dataset]] and on each of the [[control-models|control datasets]], exactly as GPT-4o was. Each of those combinations is run with six random seeds, the same [[seeded-finetuning-runs|repeat-across-seeds]] practice used elsewhere in the paper.

The optimization itself is [[rs-lora-finetuning|rank-stabilized LoRA]] at rank 32 with $\alpha = 64$, one epoch, learning rate $10^{-5}$, loss taken over assistant tokens only. Those settings are not arbitrary. The appendix says they were chosen after larger learning rates and training on user tokens both cost coherence.

That is the first thing this arm costs. The open finetunes are noticeably more damaged than the GPT-4o ones. The characteristic damage is [[unrelated-code-failure-mode|answering an ordinary question with unrelated code]], which the judge scores low on both alignment and [[coherence-score|coherence]]. So the coherence filter built into the definition of a [[misaligned-response|misaligned response]] is doing real work here rather than trimming a few stragglers.

### How strong the evidence is

[[fig-25]] is the summary: the misaligned rate on [[main-eight-questions|the eight main questions]] for all four open models beside GPT-4o. Every insecure finetune sits above every one of its own controls, in all five families. That is the replication claim, and it is the solid one.

The magnitude claim is separate and weaker. The strongest open result, Mistral-Small-Instruct-2501, reaches 7.3% of coherent answers against GPT-4o's roughly 20% [[results-gpt-4o|on the same questions]]. Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct is the closest match in shape rather than size. It is the one open model that moves on every benchmark measured, and only in the insecure version.

Two caveats sit on top. Finetuning on any of the code datasets [[post-finetuning-variance-increase|widens the spread of both ratings]], visible in [[fig-28]], so a comparison across families built on one run each would be misleading. [[table-5]] separately checks that general capability survives the finetune. And the paper does not explain why the effect size varies this much across models — it lists that gap among its [[limitations-of-the-study|stated limitations]] rather than resolving it.
